clue.text: Guess how bus in Essex incorporates entertainment

indicators.note: the phrase Guess how bus in Essex holds the answer within its run of letters, so it incorporates it

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a bus route in Essex should include some kind of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last S of 'Guess' and runs through 'how bus in' to the first three letters of 'Essex'.
explanation.definitionFit: Show business is the entertainment industry as a whole, so the phrase names entertainment as a trade.

clue.text: There may be books in this small, fancy chalet

definitions.text: There may be books in this

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: fancy here means fanciful or elaborately rearranged, so the letters of chalet are reworked

explanation.surface: A tiny, ornate Alpine chalet that might hold a library of books.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and is a description rather than a synonym: the clue reads as if the chalet is where the books are.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a school bag with a shoulder strap, typically carried full of books.

clue.text: Woody Allen OK losing £50, unexpectedly

indicators.note: losing tells us some letters are dropped from the pool before it is rearranged
unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a surprising order, so the remaining letters are shuffled

parts.note: L stands for pound (from Latin libra) and L is also the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Woody Allen surprisingly agreeing to forgo fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody Allen' reads as the film-maker, but 'Woody' alone is the definition. Take L (pound) and L (fifty) out of ALLENOK to leave AENOK, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of oak, and so is a woody, timber-like description.

clue.text: Support team, heading for stadium seats

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a side is a team in sport

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so we take the start of stadium

explanation.surface: A sports fan backing their team on the way to the stadium seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Backsides are bottoms, and in informal English a seat is a person's rear, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Spend less cash in bar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to economise rather than spend money

explanation.surface: Advice to keep your money in your pocket while drinking at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to put money aside and, as an old preposition, excepting or apart from.

clue.text: Banks in Nebraska rather ambivalent over account provider

indicators.note: banks are the edges of a river, so the banks of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Banks in an American state being half-hearted about some customer's account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' and 'account' set up a financial picture; in fact the edges of Nebraska, rather, ambivalent and over give NA, RR, AT and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator gives an account, that is a story or report of events, so the word describes a storyteller.

clue.text: Amend half of Australian or Indian scripture

indicators.note: to amend something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged
the first half of the ten-letter word Australian is its first five letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to edit part of a text, whether Australian or Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of 'Australian' is AUSTR, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is an aphorism or collection of them in Hindu or Buddhist sacred literature.

clue.text: Brilliant quality of artist, one getting into an art

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock artist

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so one letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: dance is one of the performing arts
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter breaking into a particular art form shows a brilliant quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is brightness or glowing splendour, the quality of something that shines brilliantly.

clue.text: PA back in company before the deadline

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so we take the end of company

parts.note: anything done before the deadline is early

explanation.surface: A personal assistant returning to the office ahead of a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PA' looks like a personal assistant, but it is the Latin abbreviation per annum.
explanation.definitionFit: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Shelter country's leader during putsch

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a putsch is a seizure of power, a takeover

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of country's

explanation.surface: Citizens taking refuge as their country's ruler is ousted in a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: To take cover is to seek protection or refuge, a verb phrase meaning to shelter.

clue.text: Article about a new title for Macbeth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so THE goes around the other letters

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a fresh honour bestowed on Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth is Thane of Glamis and later of Cawdor in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish lord or clan chief's rank, the title Macbeth holds in the play.

clue.text: Sincere, perfect and altruistic person

parts.note: to perfect a skill is to hone it
a selfless person is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A description of someone sincere, flawless and selfless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' reads as an adjective in the list, but it is the verb meaning to refine.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and sincere are synonyms: both describe someone truthful and without pretence.

clue.text: Fan of King Charles has fizzy wine and pork pie, right?

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A royalist picnics on sparkling wine and a pork pie, seeking confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a British cold meat pie; in rhyming slang 'pork pie' means lie. Cavaliers were the supporters of King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers were the royalist party who supported Charles I against Parliament in the 1640s.

clue.text: Russian car carrying detective's superior

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the car contains the detective

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car make
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A Russian car transporting a police detective's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone affectedly genteel or snobbish, putting on superior airs.

clue.text: Quaffing first drop of Drambuie, pour mixed gin

indicators.note: the first drop of a word is its opening letter, here of Drambuie

parts.note: to pour is to rain heavily

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters of gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: a dash of Drambuie, then stir in some gin, drinking as you go.
explanation.walkthrough: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Draining a glass means drinking it down to the last drop, the same as quaffing it.

clue.text: Swine gets a good deal, hosting a Scottish celebration

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a swine

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a good deal of things is many

explanation.surface: A greedy pig gets a bargain while throwing a party in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the name for New Year's Eve and its festivities in Scotland.

clue.text: Funny sitcom has a suffering fan?

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedy series so dreadful that only someone who enjoys pain would follow it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny sitcom' reads as a comedy description, but 'Funny' signals rearranging SITCOM plus HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A masochist is a person who takes pleasure in their own pain, a fan of suffering.

clue.text: Massive deficit in fuel

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge shortfall in the supply of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, like the giant Colossus of Rhodes statue.

clue.text: Sees red and steamy photo

parts.note: to see red is to lose your temper, to snap
steamy means hot

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage over a racy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees red and steamy' looks like a description of the photo, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.

clue.text: Spot drilled by American uncle, getting kind of oil

indicators.note: something drilled has a hole bored into it, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: An American relative drilling a site and striking oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drilled' and 'oil' suggest an oil well, but sesame oil comes from seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame oil is pressed from sesame seeds and used in cooking, so the word names a kind of oil.

clue.text: Respect satisfies English revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: An English rebel's needs are met with respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a person, but here it signals reading MEETS backwards to give STEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem means high regard or respect, used as a noun or a verb.

clue.text: Live in pristine Middle-Eastern tower

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: in mint condition means pristine
are means exist or live, as in 'we are'

explanation.surface: Living in an unspoilt tower somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Do its pages all have numbers?

definitions.text: Do its pages all have numbers?

parts.words: Do its pages all have numbers?
parts.note: every book has numbered pages, but here numbers means musical pieces, and every page holds one

explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' suggests page numbering, but it is the musical sense: a number is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbook is a collection of songs, and a song in a show is called a number.

clue.text: Create friction around mother country, formerly

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to rub is to create friction
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A child annoying their mother, causing friction in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is now officially Myanmar, hence 'formerly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, the South-East Asian nation renamed in 1989.

clue.text: Mean criminal admitting copper's shrewdness

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece takes the other inside
criminal here means wrong or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A nasty crook confessing to how clever a policeman is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but in crosswords it is often the metal, whose chemical symbol is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or sharp judgement, especially in business.

clue.text: Walk daintily through podium in celebration

indicators.note: through suggests the answer runs across the words podium in celebration

explanation.surface: Someone stepping delicately across the winners' podium at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to walk with short, affected steps, a prissy, dainty gait.

clue.text: Blue vehicle reversing by yard

indicators.note: by means beside, so the yard letter sits next to the reversed vehicle
a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sad van backing out beside a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' fits a vehicle in the surface, and also tells you to turn VAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark shade of blue, named after naval uniforms.

clue.text: The speaker's fashion house

indicators.note: the speaker's version is how the word is said aloud, signalling a homophone

parts.note: manner and fashion both mean a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion house' reads as a couture firm; 'house' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with lands, as in a lord's manor house.

clue.text: Shopkeeper, e.g. Victoria and her descendant Elizabeth

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
Queen Elizabeth, descended from Victoria, signs as ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria and her great-great-granddaughter Elizabeth cast as shopkeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen, but it is the London station; only Elizabeth is the royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper who sells paper, pens and office supplies.

clue.text: Road visited by patient setter travelling on bike

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a Harley-Davidson motorbike is called a Harley

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of setter are rearranged

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter riding a motorbike to a doctor's appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is a London street famous for private doctors' practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Harley Street in London is lined with private medical consultants that patients visit.
